description.narrative: The System Capacity Grant (SCG) Is a funding mechanism provided by GPE to support developing countries in strengthening their education systems. It is designed to help countries improve their education systems by building capacity in planning, management, monitoring, and evaluation areas, ultimately leading to better learning outcomes for children and young people. The current SCG will support Tanzania's Local Education Group (LEG) self-assessment. While UNICEF will serve as the Grant Agent for the SCG, the LEG self-assessment will fall under UNESCO as the GPE Coordinating Agent. This partnership between UNICEF and UNESCO is crucial in ensuring that education initiatives are coordinated effectively, and that the government can improve education outcomes for all children in Tanzania. By working together, UNICEF and UNESCO can leverage their respective strengths to support a more comprehensive and sustainable approach to education development in the country. The purpose of the activity is to undertake the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) Local Education Group (LEG)/ Zanzibar Education Sector Committee (ZESC) self-assessment that aims to enable the LEG to reflect on their performance, identify areas for improvement, and develop a plan for strengthening their work. This process will help to ensure that the LEG can operate more effectively and efficiently and that its efforts are aligned with the priorities and goals of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) and the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar. It also aims to support the development of a strong and sustainable education system in Zanzibar by empowering local education stakeholders to identify and address challenges in their communities.
